--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_literal_lexer_callbacks.py
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+import pytest
+
+from lark import Lark
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lexer", ["basic", "contextual"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("change_type", [False, True])
+def test_retagged_literal_callback(lexer, change_type):
+    events = []
+    def keyword(t):
+        events.append(("KEYWORD", str(t)))
+        return t.update(type="NAME" if change_type else "KEYWORD", value="literal")
+    def name(t):
+        events.append(("NAME", str(t)))
+        return t.update(value="identifier")
+    parser = Lark(
+        'start: (KEYWORD | NAME)+\nKEYWORD: "if"\nNAME: /[a-z]+/\n%ignore " "',
+        parser="lalr", lexer=lexer,
+        lexer_callbacks={"KEYWORD": keyword, "NAME": name},
+    )
+    tree = parser.parse("if word")
+    assert events == [("KEYWORD", "if"), ("NAME", "word")]
+    assert [(t.type, str(t)) for t in tree.children] == [
+        ("NAME" if change_type else "KEYWORD", "literal"),
+        ("NAME", "identifier"),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_retagging_without_literal_callback():
+    events = []
+    def name(t):
+        events.append(str(t))
+        return t
+    parser = Lark(
+        'start: (KEYWORD | NAME)+\nKEYWORD: "if"\nNAME: /[a-z]+/\n%ignore " "',
+        parser="lalr", lexer="basic", lexer_callbacks={"NAME": name},
+    )
+    tree = parser.parse("if word")
+    assert events == ["word"]
+    assert tree.children == ["if", "word"]
spec.notes: The hidden tests use equal-priority overlapping literal and regex terminals. They check literal dispatch, regex dispatch, absence of callback cascades, and the no-literal-callback case. Existing position and callback tests should continue to pass.
spec.question: Explicit lexer callbacks should work for literal tokens even when the basic scanner embeds those literals in a regex terminal. For non-ignored tokens, if `UnlessCallback` retags a regex match as a literal terminal, invoke that literal terminal's configured `lexer_callbacks` callback exactly once, and do not invoke the regex terminal's user callback. If the literal has no configured callback, return the retagged token unchanged. A user callback changing the token type must not trigger another user callback. Preserve ordinary regex callback behavior and token coordinates, and make this work with both `lexer='basic'` and `lexer='contextual'`. Deliver a unified diff against production files only.
